what_its_for: This ear drop medicine treats bacterial ear infections. It combines an antibiotic (ciprofloxacin) that kills bacteria with a steroid (dexamethasone) that reduces swelling, redness, and discomfort in the ear. It is used for infections of the middle ear (in children with ear tubes) and infections of the outer ear canal (commonly called swimmer's ear) in adults and children.
how_to_take: Use this medicine only in the ear — never in the eye or by mouth. Wash your hands before and after using the drops. Warm the bottle by holding it in your hand for 1 to 2 minutes before using — cold drops can cause dizziness. Gently shake the bottle well before each use. Lie down or tilt your head so the affected ear faces up. For outer ear infections: gently pull the outer ear up and back (for adults) or down and back (for young children) to straighten the ear canal, then place the drops in the ear. For middle ear infections with ear tubes: just place the drops directly into the ear canal. After putting in the drops, press gently on the small flap of skin in front of the ear opening (the tragus) 4 times to help the drops reach deeper into the ear. Stay in position for at least 60 seconds. Repeat in the other ear if instructed by your doctor. Do not touch the dropper tip to your ear or any surface to keep it clean.
dosing: The usual dose is 4 drops in the affected ear(s) twice a day (once in the morning and once in the evening), for 7 days. Always follow the exact instructions from your doctor or pharmacist. Do not use more drops or use them more often than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use the drops as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not double up on doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store the bottle at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Do not freeze. Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children. Throw away any unused drops after you finish your full course of treatment or after the expiration date on the bottle, whichever comes first. Do not save leftover drops for future ear problems without talking to your doctor.
what_to_avoid: Do not use these drops in your eyes — they are for the ear only. Do not use cotton wicks or plugs in your ear unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid getting water in your ear during treatment when possible; try to keep your ear dry while swimming or bathing by using a waterproof earplug (ask your doctor first). Do not share this medicine with anyone else. Do not stop using it early just because your ear feels better — finish the full 7-day course to make sure the infection is fully treated.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if: your symptoms do not start to improve after a few days of treatment, or get worse at any time; you notice a rash, hives, or itching in or around the ear; you experience severe ear pain, drainage that increases, or a new fever; you have any signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat, difficulty breathing, or severe rash; you accidentally get the drops in your eye; or you have concerns about your child's ear tubes during treatment.
when_it_works: Most people begin to feel some relief from pain and discomfort within the first 1 to 2 days of treatment. However, it is very important to use all 7 days of drops even if you feel better sooner, to fully clear the infection and prevent it from coming back.
special_populations: Children: This medicine is approved for use in children 6 months of age and older. Use the same dose as adults (4 drops twice daily) unless your child's doctor tells you otherwise. Always pull the ear down and back (rather than up and back) when giving drops to young children. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before using this medicine. The safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established, so use only if your doctor determines the benefit outweighs any potential risk. Older adults: No special dose adjustments are typically needed, but always follow your doctor's instructions.
